claim: Formation of membraneless organelles or biological condensates via phase separation and related processes hugely expands the cellular organelle repertoire.
source: Formation of membraneless organelles or biological condensates via phase separation and related processes hugely expands the cellular organelle repertoire.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract summarizing the general significance of biological condensates.

claim: Biological condensates are dense and viscoelastic soft matters instead of canonical dilute solutions.
source: Biological condensates are dense and viscoelastic soft matters instead of canonical dilute solutions.
evidence: This is a characterization statement in the abstract describing the physical nature of biological condensates.

claim: Molecules in the condensed phase do not undergo uniform Brownian motion, but instead constantly switch between a (class of) confined state(s) and a random diffusion-like motion state.
source: Notably, molecules in the condensed phase do not undergo uniform Brownian motion, but instead constantly switch between a (class of) confined state(s) and a random diffusion-like motion state.
evidence: This is a key finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental observations throughout the manuscript.

claim: Transient confinement is consistent with strong interactions associated with large molecular networks (i.e., percolation) in the condensed phase.
source: Transient confinement is consistent with strong interactions associated with large molecular networks (i.e., percolation) in the condensed phase.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings provided in the abstract.

claim: Molecules in biological condensates behave distinctly different from those in dilute solutions.
source: In this way, molecules in biological condensates behave distinctly different from those in dilute solutions.
evidence: This is a conclusion stated in the abstract based on the observed motion properties.

claim: Phase separation-mediated formation of condensed macro-molecular assemblies is being increasingly recognized as a general mechanism for cells to form a distinct class of cellular organelles with diverse functions.
source: Phase separation-mediated formation of condensed macro-molecular assemblies is being increasingly recognized as a general mechanism for cells to form a distinct class of cellular organelles with diverse functions (Banani et al., 2017; Chen et al., 2020; Lyon et al., 2021; Shin et al., 2017; Wu et al., 2020).
evidence: This statement is supported by multiple citations to prior literature.

claim: Organelles formed via phase separation either do not associate with or are not enclosed by lipid membranes.
source: Compared to the classical cellular organelles that are demarcated by lipid membranes, organelles formed via phase separation either do not associate with or are not enclosed by lipid membranes.
evidence: This is a defining characteristic of biological condensates stated in the introduction.

claim: Molecules within biological condensates can be in relatively fast dynamic exchange with their counterparts in dilute solution without energy input.
source: Since biological condensates are not enclosed by membranes, molecules within biological condensates can be in relatively fast dynamic exchange with their counterparts in dilute solution without energy input.
evidence: This is a property inferred from the lack of membrane enclosure.

claim: Proteins can be concentrated by more than 10,000 folds upon chromatin condensate formation.
source: For example, proteins can be concentrated by more than 10,000 folds upon chromatin condensate formation (Gibson et al., 2019).
evidence: This is a specific example cited from prior literature.

claim: Phase separation can concentrate numerous proteins into postsynaptic densities by >1000-fold.
source: In cell peripherals such as synapses in neurons, phase separation can concentrate numerous proteins into postsynaptic densities by >1000-fold (Zeng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a specific example cited from prior literature.

claim: A biological condensate formed via phase separation is more of a condensed soft matter system, thus theories dealing with dilute solutions are not expected to be generally adequate for condensed molecular systems.
source: A biological condensate formed via phase separation is more of a condensed soft matter system, thus theories dealing with dilute solutions are not expected to be generally adequate for condensed molecular systems.
evidence: This is a reasoning statement about the applicability of existing theories.

claim: The PSD mixtures formed noncircular condensed phase on SLB with around or less than 1 μm in size.
source: The PSD mixtures formed noncircular condensed phase on SLB with around or less than 1 μm in size, but conventional TIRF images could only provide fuzzy phase boundaries at this scale (Figure 1B, top; see also [Zeng et al., 2018]).
evidence: This is an observation from the experiments, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The partition coefficient of NR2B is 60.8 ± 1.6.
source: Comparing the average localization densities in the condensed and dilute phases, we could estimate the partition coefficient of 60.8 ± 1.6 for NR2B (i.e., NR2B was enriched into the condense phase by ~61-folds).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement derived from super-resolution imaging data.

claim: The distribution of NR2B in the condensed phase is not homogeneous.
source: We noted with interest that the distribution of NR2B in the condensed phase is not homogeneous (Figure 1C), indicating possible formation of nanodomain-like clusters within the condensed phase.
evidence: This is an observation from Figure 1C.

claim: The existence of nanodomain-like NR2B clusters in the condensed phase is supported by autocorrelation function analysis of NR2B distributions.
source: The existence of nanodomain-like NR2B clusters in the condensed phase is supported by autocorrelation function analysis of NR2B distributions (Tang et al., 2016; Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by data analysis shown in supplementary figures and cited methodology.

claim: The initial roughly estimated overall diffusion coefficients of NR2B in condensed phase and dilute phase are 0.22 μm2/s and 0.57 μm2/s, respectively.
source: The initial roughly estimated overall diffusion coefficients of NR2B in condensed phase and dilute phase are 0.22 μm2/s and 0.57 μm2/s, respectively (see analyses below).
evidence: This is a preliminary quantitative measurement from the tracking algorithm.

claim: The number of NR2B molecules entering into and escaping from the condensed phase was equal.
source: The number of NR2B molecules entering into and escaping from the condensed phase was equal (Figure 2D), a finding that is consistent with the bulk equilibrium state of the PSD condensate.
evidence: This is an experimental observation shown in Figure 2D and interpreted as evidence of equilibrium.

claim: NR2B molecules within the condensed phase spent a large proportion of time in the confined state and molecules could switch between the confined state and the mobile state.
source: Interestingly, NR2B molecules within the condensed phase spent a large proportion of time in the confined state and molecules could switch between the confined state and the mobile state (Figure 2C and E, Video 1).
evidence: This is a direct observation from tracking data shown in figures and video.

claim: No confined state could be detected when only NR2B was tethered to SLB.
source: No confined state could be detected when only NR2B was tethered to SLB (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a control experiment result shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: The transient kinetic trapping of NR2B in the PSD condensed phase is likely due to its relatively strong binding to certain parts of a percolated PSD network with slow dynamics.
source: Comparisons with data from a set of model experimental systems of FUS-Shank3 chimeric proteins (see Figure 4) suggest that the transient kinetic trapping of NR2B (transiently remaining very close to a stationary position, i.e., very slow diffusion) in the PSD condensed phase is likely due to its relatively strong binding to certain parts of a percolated PSD network with slow dynamics.
evidence: This is an interpretation based on comparison with model systems.

claim: NR2B molecules in the condensed phase are expected to undergo subdiffusive motions.
source: Accordingly, NR2B molecules in the condensed phase are expected to undergo subdiffusive motions.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the observed transient trapping behavior.

claim: Single-molecule tracking data of NR2B motion in the condensed PSD phase fits well with typical behaviors of subdiffusion.
source: Indeed, our single-molecule tracking data of NR2B motion in the condensed PSD phase (see Figure 2E for an example) fits well with typical behaviors of subdiffusion (see below and Berezhkovskii et al., 2014; Bouchaud and Georges, 1990; Condamin et al., 2008; Netz and Dorfmüller, 1995; Saxton, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data and cited theoretical frameworks.

claim: In the condensed phase, each NR2B molecule spent a large proportion of time in the confined state in a manner similar to that for the 2D case.
source: We also imaged motions of NR2B in the PSD condensates formed in 3D solution at single-molecular resolution and found that, in the condensed phase, each NR2B molecule spent a large proportion of time in the confined state in a manner similar to that for the 2D case (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation from 3D imaging experiments.

claim: The histogram of NR2B displacement tracks in the condensed PSD phase has a dominant peak with very small displacements, corresponding to the large proportion of time NR2B spends in a confined state or an ensemble of confined states.
source: The histogram of NR2B displacement tracks in the condensed PSD phase has a dominant peak with very small displacements, corresponding to the large proportion of time NR2B spends in a confined state or an ensemble of confined states.
evidence: This is a description of the displacement distribution data.

claim: A small and relatively flat shoulder tailing the main peak represents the small proportion of time NR2B is in a mobile state or an ensemble of mobile states moving with larger displacements during the same given time interval.
source: In contrast, a small and relatively flat shoulder tailing the main peak represents the small proportion of time NR2B is in a mobile state or an ensemble of mobile states moving with larger displacements during the same given time interval (Figure 3A1).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the displacement distribution shown in Figure 3A1.

claim: Fitting the histogram with a single population of NR2B undergoing Brownian motion could only cover the confined state peak of molecule but not the high-displacement tail of this distribution.
source: Fitting the histogram with a single population of NR2B undergoing Brownian motion could only cover the confined state peak of molecule but not the high-displacement tail of this distribution (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C1).
evidence: This is a result from fitting analysis shown in a supplementary figure.

claim: In the dilute phase, the overall displacements of NR2B are much larger as well as broader, and there is no prominent peak at very small displacements.
source: By comparison, in the dilute phase, the overall displacements of NR2B are much larger as well as broader, and there is no prominent peak at very small displacements (Figure 3A2).
evidence: This is an observation from displacement distribution data in the dilute phase.

claim: The displacement histogram of NR2B in the dilute PSD phase still cannot be described entirely by simple Brownian diffusion of a homogeneous NR2B population.
source: Nonetheless, the displacement histogram of NR2B in the dilute PSD phase still cannot be described entirely by simple Brownian diffusion of a homogeneous NR2B population (Figure 3—figure supplement 1C2), though a simple Brownian diffusion is a better approximation in this case, suggesting a likely presence of multiple populations/states of pre-percolated NR2B/PSD protein complexes even in the dilute phase, a feature that would be in line with recent observations that some subsaturated solutions of condensate-forming biomolecules are not featureless (Kar et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an observation from fitting analysis with interpretation citing recent literature.

claim: In a control system with only NR2B tethered to SLB, the histogram of NR2B displacements can be reasonably fitted by a simple diffusion model.
source: However, in a control system with only NR2B tethered to SLB (i.e., no addition of any other PSD proteins), the histogram of NR2B displacements can be reasonably fitted by a simple diffusion model (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a result from a control experiment shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The resulting best-fit diffusion coefficients in the presumed mobile and confined states were, respectively, Dm = 0.167 ± 0.002 μm2/s and Dc = 0.0127 ± 0.0001 μm2/s.
source: The resulting best-fit diffusion coefficients in the presumed mobile and confined states were, respectively, Dm = 0.167 ± 0.002 μm2/s and Dc = 0.0127 ± 0.0001 μm2/s.
evidence: These are quantitative parameters obtained from HMM fitting.

claim: The switching probabilities between these presumed states were Pmc = 82.8% ± 0.3% (mobile to confined states) per frame and Pcm = 3.8% ± 0.1% (confined to mobile states) per frame.
source: The switching probabilities between these presumed states were Pmc = 82.8% ± 0.3% (mobile to confined states) per frame and Pcm = 3.8% ± 0.1% (confined to mobile states) per frame.
evidence: These are quantitative parameters obtained from HMM fitting.

claim: For NR2B in the present model for PSD condensates, Pc = 95.6%.
source: For NR2B in the present model for PSD condensates, Pc = 95.6%.
evidence: This is a calculated value based on the switching probabilities.

claim: The mobile ratio is Pm = 1-Pc = 4.4%.
source: The mobile ratio, defined as the percentage of time that a molecule spends in the mobile state, could then be calculated as Pm = 1-Pc = 4.4%.
evidence: This is a calculated value based on the confinement ratio.

claim: The fitted diffusion coefficient of presumed simple diffusion of NR2B in the dilute phase of the present PSD condensate is 0.47 ± 0.12 μm2/s.
source: The fitted diffusion coefficient of presumed simple diffusion of NR2B in the dilute phase of the present PSD condensate is 0.47 ± 0.12 μm2/s, which is close to that of NR2B alone tethered to SLB (0.61 ± 0.04 μm2/s) (Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from MSD fitting shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The overall generalized diffusion coefficient for subdiffusion of NR2B in the PSD condensed phase is Dα = 0.014 ± 0.001 μm2/s0.74 with α = 0.74 ± 0.03.
source: The quantitative similarity of these two estimated diffusion coefficients is particularly striking in view of the much lower diffusion rate reflected by the overall generalized diffusion coefficient for subdiffusion of NR2B in the PSD condensed phase (Dα = 0.014 ± 0.001 μm2/s0.74 with α = 0.74 ± 0.03; see Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement from subdiffusive model fitting shown in Figure 3E.

claim: The EF of NR2B in the condensed phase estimated via the approximate relation in Equation 1 by using these experimental kinetic parameters is Dd/PmDm = 62.8.
source: It follows that the EF of NR2B in the condensed phase estimated via the approximate relation in Equation 1 by using these experimental kinetic parameters is Dd/PmDm = 62.8.
evidence: This is a calculated value based on experimental parameters and the derived equation.

claim: The kinetics-estimated EF is very close to the equilibrium value of ~61 derived independently from experimentally observed localizations.
source: Since this kinetics-estimated EF is very close to the equilibrium value of ~61 derived independently from experimentally observed localizations (Figure 1B), we regard Equation 1 as empirically validated for the present PSD system, although the relationship between kinetic and thermodynamic properties of diffusive systems (Berry et al., 2018) can be rather complex in general for rugged energy landscapes (Banerjee et al., 2014; Zwanzig, 1988).
evidence: This is a comparison between calculated and measured values, with citations to relevant theory.

claim: The energy barrier at the interface between the condensed and dilute phases is likely not large in this system.
source: Because we did not observe any obvious hindrance against motions when molecules cross the phase boundaries (Figure 3—figure supplement 2), the energy barrier at the interface between the condensed and dilute phases is likely not large in this system (Brangwynne et al., 2011; Feric et al., 2016), though diffusion barriers at phase boundaries were reported in other systems (Peng and Weber, 2019; Strom et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an inference from experimental observations with citations to related findings in other systems.

claim: When the experiment-based, HMM-estimated Dd = 0.47 μm2/s, Dm = 0.17 μm2/s, Pmc = 0.828, Pcm = 0.038 (per 30 ms), and thus Pm = 4.4% values were applied to the Monte Carlo setup, it yielded a simulated EF = 62.2 ± 0.3.
source: When the experiment-based, HMM-estimated Dd = 0.47 μm2/s, Dm = 0.17 μm2/s, Pmc = 0.828, Pcm = 0.038 (per 30 ms), and thus Pm = 4.4% values (see above) were applied to the same Monte Carlo setup, it yielded a simulated EF = 62.2 ± 0.3 (uncertainty based on 10 independent runs with different random seeds), which is practically identical to the EF value of 62.8 estimated by Equation 1.
evidence: This is a result from Monte Carlo simulation using experimental parameters.

claim: The PrLD-SAMWT chimera could undergo phase separation at very low concentrations.
source: Thus, the PrLD-SAM chimera contains a weak and multivalent interaction domain and a specific and multivalent interaction domain within one protein. The PrLD-SAM chimera could undergo phase separation at very low concentrations (see below), so we 'caged' the chimera with highly soluble maltose binding protein (MBP) at its N-terminus and a small, highly soluble protein GB1 at its C-terminus (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is an experimental observation about the phase separation behavior of the chimeric protein.

claim: The PrLD-SAMWT chimera underwent phase separation at concentration as low as 1 μM.
source: The PrLD-SAMWT chimera underwent phase separation at concentration as low as 1 μM.
evidence: This is a quantitative experimental observation.

claim: The threshold phase separation concentrations for PrLD-SAMME and PrLD were much higher (~150 μM and ~250 μM, respectively).
source: In contrast, the threshold phase separation concentrations for PrLD-SAMME and PrLD were much higher (~150 μM and ~250 μM, respectively).
evidence: These are quantitative experimental observations.

claim: Specific and multivalent interactions act in concert in the PrLD-SAMWT condensate, and such multivalent interactions can dramatically lower the threshold concentration of phase separation.
source: These results demonstrate that specific and multivalent interactions act in concert in the PrLD-SAMWT condensate, and such multivalent interactions can dramatically lower the threshold concentration of phase separation (Espinosa et al., 2020; Lin et al., 2022; Riback et al., 2020; Zeng et al., 2018; Zeng et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data with citations to supporting literature.

claim: PrLD-SAMWT molecule spent most of their time (74.0 ± 3.7%) in the transiently confined state.
source: HMM analyses of experimental data indicate that PrLD-SAMWT molecule spent most of their time (74.0 ± 3.7%) in the transiently confined state, though these molecules were able to switch between the confined and mobile states (Figure 4E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from HMM analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: PrLD-SAMME spent 98.1 ± 1.8% of time in the mobile state and PrLD spent 99.6 ± 0.4% in the mobile state.
source: In contrast, the mobilities of PrLD-SAMME or PrLD in the condensed phase were much higher. PrLD-SAMME spent 98.1 ± 1.8% of time in the mobile state and PrLD spent 99.6 ± 0.4% in the mobile state (Figure 4E).
evidence: These are quantitative results from HMM analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The HMM-estimated diffusion coefficients of PrLD-SAMWT and PrLD-SAMME in their mobile state were very similar (0.18 ± 0.05 μm2/s vs. 0.19 ± 0.02 μm2/s).
source: Interestingly, the HMM-estimated diffusion coefficients of PrLD-SAMWT and PrLD-SAMME in their mobile state were very similar (0.18 ± 0.05 μm2/s vs. 0.19 ± 0.02 μm2/s) (Figure 4E), indicating that PrLD-SAMWT and PrLD-SAMME have similar effective molecular sizes in their mobile state.
evidence: These are quantitative results from HMM analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: The diffusion coefficient of the mobile state of PrLD is estimated by HMM to be 0.36 ± 0.04 μm2/s.
source: The diffusion coefficient of the mobile state of PrLD is estimated by HMM to be 0.36 ± 0.04 μm2/s (Figure 4E) and the molecular weight of PrLD is about half of PrLD-SAMWT and PrLD-SAMME, again suggesting that the mobile state of PrLD likely corresponds to the network-unbound form of PrLD.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from HMM analysis shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Strong multivalent interactions tend to lead to formation of large and more stable molecular networks in the condensed phase, which could dramatically reduce the overall motions of the molecules in the condensed phase.
source: Taken together, the above single-molecule tracking study of our designed FUS PrLD systems buttressed our general hypothesis that strong multivalent interactions tend to lead to formation of large and more stable molecular networks in the condensed phase, which could dramatically reduce the overall motions of the molecules in the condensed phase.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experimental data on the designed systems.

claim: In condensed phases formed by weakly interacting IDR sequences, the molecular networks in the condensed phase are much more dynamic/transient and likely much smaller in spatial extent, thus resulting in IDR proteins displaying simple diffusion-like behaviors.
source: By comparison, in condensed phases formed by weakly interacting IDR sequences, the molecular networks in the condensed phase are much more dynamic/transient and likely much smaller in spatial extent, thus resulting in IDR proteins displaying simple diffusion-like behaviors.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparison of the different experimental systems.

claim: The PrLD system showed the fastest recovery speed, and the PrLD-SAMME system showed a slightly slower recover speed.
source: The PrLD system showed the fastest recovery speed, and the PrLD-SAMME system showed a slightly slower recover speed.
evidence: This is an observation from FRAP experiments.

claim: The PrLD-SAMWT system, with its large and stable molecular network in the condensed phase, displayed a very slow and near linear recovery curve.
source: The PrLD-SAMWT system, with its large and stable molecular network in the condensed phase, displayed a very slow and near linear recovery curve (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is an observation from FRAP experiments shown in Figure 5F.

claim: The simulated FRAP curves were overall very similar to those obtained experimentally.
source: The simulated FRAP curves were overall very similar to those obtained experimentally (Figure 5G vs. F), notwithstanding a faster recovery rate in the simulated curve vs. the experimental curve for the PrLD-SAMWT system that is likely due to overestimations of the mobile ratio of the protein in the tracking experiment.
evidence: This is a comparison between simulation and experimental results shown in Figures 5F and 5G.

claim: The FRAP curve of a molecular species in a phase separation system is heavily influenced by the proportion of time of the molecules that are transiently trapped in the confined state.
source: Taken together, the above theoretical and experimental studies revealed that the FRAP curve of a molecular species in a phase separation system is heavily influenced by the proportion of time of the molecules that are transiently trapped in the confined state, a parameter directly linked to the strong and specific multivalent interactions of the system.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the combined theoretical and experimental FRAP studies.

claim: A low recovery rate in the FRAP assay does not necessarily mean that a large fraction of molecules in the condensed phase is permanently immobile.
source: Accordingly, a low recovery rate in the FRAP assay does not necessarily mean that a large fraction of molecules in the condensed phase is permanently immobile.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the FRAP analysis.

claim: The most notable direct experimental finding from our study is that molecules in the condensed phase of biological condensates do not exhibit simple diffusion behaviors as those observed in dilute solutions.
source: Applying this technique to PSD, the most notable direct experimental finding from our study is that molecules in the condensed phase of biological condensates do not exhibit simple diffusion behaviors as those observed in dilute solutions.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the key experimental finding.

claim: Molecules appear to constantly switch between a broadly construed transient confined state and a broadly construed mobile state in the condensed phase.
source: Instead, molecules appear to constantly switch between a broadly construed transient confined state and a broadly construed mobile state in the condensed phase.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the key experimental finding.

claim: This two-state-like phenomenon of condensed-phase motion is most likely underpinned by phase separation-mediated formation of large and percolated molecular networks.
source: This two-state-like phenomenon of condensed-phase motion is most likely underpinned by phase separation-mediated formation of large and percolated molecular networks.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: The size and dynamic properties of the molecular network in the condensed phase are necessarily determined by the binding affinity (or affinities) and valence of the interaction(s) of the molecule(s) in the phase separation system.
source: The size and dynamic properties of the molecular network in the condensed phase are necessarily determined by the binding affinity (or affinities) and valence of the interaction(s) of the molecule(s) in the phase separation system, a trend that has been recently predicted by theoretical simulations treating biomolecules as associative polymers (Choi et al., 2020; Harmon et al., 2017; Pappu et al., 2023) and illustrated by the model PrLD-SAMWT system examined here.
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by experimental data and cited theoretical predictions.

claim: For biological condensates assembled largely by strong and specific molecular interactions, molecules in the condensed phase spend most of their time in the confined state.
source: For biological condensates assembled largely by strong and specific molecular interactions (including condensates formed with combinations of strong molecular interactions with IDR sequence-based weak interactions; Chen et al., 2020; Feng et al., 2021; see Lin et al., 2022 for more discussions), molecules in the condensed phase spend most of their time in the confined state.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the experimental data with citations to related work.

claim: Phase separation-mediated formation of biological condensates is a very powerful means for cells to form numerous subcellular organelles with a continuum of dynamic and material properties ranging from very dynamic, dilute solution-like assemblies to highly stable, solid-like systems.
source: In this light, phase separation-mediated formation of biological condensates is further revealed to be a very powerful means indeed for cells to form numerous subcellular organelles with a continuum of dynamic and material properties ranging from very dynamic, dilute solution-like assemblies to highly stable, solid-like systems.
evidence: This is a broader implication drawn from the findings.

claim: Confinements of molecules in cellular condensates have been observed by single-molecule tracking experiments recently.
source: Confinements of molecules in cellular condensates have been observed by single-molecule tracking experiments recently (Chong et al., 2022; Miné-Hattab et al., 2021; Niewidok et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a statement citing recent observations in the literature.

claim: The two motion states in our simple two-state model for condensed-phase dynamics should be understood to be consisting of multiple substates.
source: With this in mind, the two motion states in our simple two-state model for condensed-phase dynamics should be understood to be consisting of multiple substates.
evidence: This is a clarification about the interpretation of the model.

claim: Molecular motions in the percolated condensed phase likely cover a continuum of mobilities.
source: It follows that molecular motions in the percolated condensed phase likely cover a continuum of mobilities, although the confined- and mobile-state diffusion coefficients deduced from our experimental measurements based on the two-state model do represent two important time scales of intra-condensate dynamics of PSD.
evidence: This is an interpretation acknowledging the complexity beyond the simple two-state model.

claim: The dynamic network properties and consequently the functions of organelles formed via phase separation may be regulated in ways that are distinctly different from those occurring in dilute solutions.
source: Since the interactions between molecules can be modulated via numerous cellular processes such as posttranslational modifications, protein biogenesis/turnovers, epigenetic modification, cellular milieu alterations, etc., the dynamic network properties and consequently the functions of organelles formed via phase separation may be regulated in ways that are distinctly different from those occurring in dilute solutions.
evidence: This is a speculation about the functional implications of the findings.

claim: Few satisfying theoretical frameworks have been established for the condensed assemblies formed via phase separation in cells.
source: Compared to the rich knowledge and quantitative theories for dilute-solution systems, few satisfying theoretical frameworks have been established for the condensed assemblies formed via phase separation in cells (see Mittag and Pappu, 2022 and refs therein), partly due to our poor understandings of microscopic motion properties of molecules in the condensed phase.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of the field with citation.

claim: Biological phase separation research that focuses primarily on IDRs has only touched the tip of the iceberg.
source: The dramatic dynamic and material property differences of condensates formed by weakly associative intrinsically disordered proteins and by biomolecules with strongly favorable specific interactions involving folded domains indicate that biological phase separation research that focuses primarily on IDRs has only touched the tip of the iceberg.
evidence: This is a perspective statement about the scope of the field.
